name: Claude Code v2.1.243 — Released Today; modelPicker, 1-Hour Cache Tuning, 340 MB → 75 MB Binary, 40–70 MB Less Memory
hook: Released August 25: the biggest single Claude Code drop in weeks. New `modelPicker` setting lets you curate /model with an ordered, labeled list of any model ID including Vertex and Bedrock spellings. `promptCacheTtl` + `subagentPromptCacheTtl` decouple cache strategy — keep 1-hour prompt cache on the main conversation while subagents run at 5 min; for API-key and cloud-provider users this is a direct cost lever. `modelPricing` managed setting replaces list price with your org's contracted rates in /cost, the status line, and telemetry. Keyless sign-in via Console account joins the API-key path. Linux binary now zstd-compressed: ~75 MB download instead of ~340 MB. Sessions use 40–70 MB less RAM with improved GC. Startup is faster — sandbox and MCP bring-up no longer block the first frame. Loops breakdown added to /usage: per-loop run count, total tokens, tokens per run, last run. 30+ bug fixes, including dropped MCP connections in non-interactive sessions now auto-reconnecting. v2.1.245 (same day) patches a startup crash on glibc 2.44 distros (Arch, CachyOS, Fedora Rawhide).

name: Boris Cherny at YC Startup School — Anthropic Deleted 80% of Claude Code's System Prompt. The Model Got Smarter.
hook: Published fresh off Opus 5's launch, Claude Code creator Boris Cherny told YC Startup School that Anthropic stripped more than 80% of Claude Code's system prompt when Opus 5 arrived — and the model performed better without the scaffolding, not worse. Cherny's argument: the entire AI dev-tools industry is building products for yesterday's weaker models. Frontier models today can handle harder tasks with fewer instructions, and over-prompting is actively handicapping them. The talk also covers why Cherny hasn't written a line of code in months, how Opus 5 hit 30% on ARC-AGI, and why cost-per-task comparisons are the wrong frame.
